spots.name: York Minster

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: York Minster, formally the Cathedral and Metropolitical Church of St Peter in York, is an Anglican cathedral in the city of York, North Yorkshire, England.

spots.name: The Shambles
spots.summary: The Shambles is a historic street in York, England, featuring preserved medieval buildings, some dating to the 14th century. Running between Newgate in the north and Pavement in the south, the street is narrow, with many timber-framed buildings with jettied floors which overhang the street by several feet.

spots.name: York Castle
spots.summary: York Castle is a fortified complex in the city of York, England. It consists of a sequence of castles, prisons, law courts and other buildings, which were built over the last nine centuries on the north-west side of the River Foss.

spots.name: National Railway Museum
spots.summary: The National Railway Museum (NRM) is a museum in York, England, forming part of the Science Museum Group. The museum tells the story of rail transport in Britain and its impact on society.

spots.name: Eboracum

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Eboracum was a fort and later a city in the Roman province of Britannia. In its prime it was the largest town in northern Britannia and a provincial capital. The site remained occupied after the decline of the Western Roman Empire and ultimately developed into the present-day city of York, in North Yorkshire, England.

spots.name: York city walls
spots.summary: York has, since Roman times, been defended by walls of one form or another. To this day, substantial portions of the walls remain, and York has more miles of intact wall than any other city in England. They are known variously as York City Walls, the Bar Walls and the Roman walls.

spots.name: York railway station
spots.summary: York railway station is a principal stop on the East Coast Main Line (ECML) serving the cathedral city of York, in North Yorkshire, England. It is 188 miles 40 chains (303.4 km) north of London King's Cross and, on the main line, it is situated between Doncaster to the south and Thirsk to the north.

spots.name: Jorvik Viking Centre
spots.summary: Jorvik Viking Centre is a museum and visitor attraction in York, England, containing lifelike mannequins and life-size dioramas depicting Viking life in the city. Visitors are taken through the dioramas in 'time capsule' carriages equipped with speakers. It was created by York Archaeological Trust and opened in 1984.

spots.name: Whip-Ma-Whop-Ma-Gate
spots.summary: Whip-Ma-Whop-Ma-Gate is a street in York, England, known for its short length and unusual name. A continuation of Colliergate, it runs south to meet Pavement, Fossgate, and the Stonebow, a distance of perhaps 80 feet (24 m), and is adjoined by St Saviourgate on its eastern side.

spots.name: St Mary's Abbey, York

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Abbey of St Mary is a ruined Benedictine abbey in York, England and a scheduled monument.

spots.name: York Museum Gardens
spots.summary: The York Museum Gardens are botanic gardens in the centre of York, England, beside the River Ouse. They cover an area of 10 acres (4.0 ha) of the former grounds of St Mary's Abbey, and were created in the 1830s by the Yorkshire Philosophical Society along with the Yorkshire Museum which they contain.

spots.name: Yorkshire Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Yorkshire Museum is a museum in York, England. It was opened in 1830, and has five permanent collections, covering biology, geology, archaeology, numismatics and astronomy.

spots.name: Treasurer's House, York
spots.summary: The Treasurer's House in York, North Yorkshire, England, is a Grade I listed historic house owned by the National Trust, who also maintain its garden. It is located in Minster Yard, directly to the north of York Minster.

spots.name: St Michael le Belfrey, York

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Michael le Belfrey is an Anglican church in York, England. It is situated at the junction of High Petergate and Minster Yard, directly opposite York Minster, in the centre of the city.

spots.name: Church of Holy Trinity

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Sun

spots.summary: Holy Trinity Church, on Goodramgate in York, is a Grade I listed former parish church in the Church of England in York and is in the care of the Churches Conservation Trust.

spots.name: York Castle Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The York Castle Museum is a museum located in York, North Yorkshire, England, on the site of York Castle, which was originally built by William the Conqueror in 1068. The museum itself was founded by John L.

spots.name: Stonegate
spots.summary: Stonegate is a street in the city centre of York, England, one of the streets most visited by tourists. Most of the buildings along the street are listed, meaning they are of national importance due to their architecture or history.

spots.name: Pavement
spots.summary: Pavement is a street in the city centre of York, England.

spots.name: Statue of Elizabeth II
spots.summary: A statue of Queen Elizabeth II was unveiled at York Minster on 9 November 2022 by King Charles III, two months after the Queen's death in September 2022. The 6ft 7in (2m) tall sculpture was intended to mark the late monarch's Platinum Jubilee and was completed in August 2022, a month before her death.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Statue of Elizabeth II, York Minster

spots.name: York Oratory
spots.summary: The Oratory Church of Saint Wilfrid, York is a Catholic church in York, England. A church dedicated to Saint Wilfrid has stood in York since medieval times. It is within the Diocese of Middlesbrough and was the second pro-Cathedral of the Diocese of Beverley until its dissolution in 1878.

spots.name: Golden Fleece, York
spots.summary: The Golden Fleece is an inn on Pavement in York, England, with a free house pub on the ground floor and four guest bedrooms above. It dates back to at least the early 16th century, although the present building is a rebuild from around 1840. The pub claims to be the most haunted in the city.

spots.name: Barley Hall
spots.summary: Barley Hall is a Grade II listed reconstructed medieval townhouse on Coffee Yard in the city of York, England. It was built around 1360 by the monks of Nostell Priory near Wakefield and extended in the 15th century.

spots.name: York Art Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue

spots.summary: York Art Gallery is a public art gallery on Exhibition Square in York, England, with a collection of paintings from 14th-century to contemporary, prints, watercolours, drawings, and ceramics. It closed for major redevelopment in 2013, reopening in summer of 2015.

spots.name: Merchant Adventurers' Hall
spots.summary: The Merchant Adventurers' Hall is a medieval guildhall on Fossgate in the city of York, England. It is a Grade I listed building and scheduled ancient monument.

spots.name: Fairfax House

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: Fairfax House is a Georgian townhouse on Castlegate in York, England, near Clifford's Tower and York Castle Museum.

spots.name: York Guildhall
spots.summary: The York Guildhall is a municipal building in St Martins Courtyard on Coney Street in York, England. Located behind the Mansion House, it is a Grade I listed building.

spots.name: Baile Hill

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Baile Hill is a man-made earth mound in the Bishophill area of York, England. It is the only remaining feature of the fortification known as the Old Baile.

spots.name: Anglian Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Anglian Tower is the lower portion of an early medieval tower on the city walls of York, England. It is located on the south-west (interior) face of the city walls, currently in the grounds of York City Library and accessible on foot both from there and the Museum Gardens.

spots.name: York Dungeon

hours.note: Closed Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: York Dungeon is a tourist attraction in York, England. York Dungeon depicts history of the dungeon using actor led shows, special effects and displays of models and objects.

spots.name: Ye Olde Starre Inne
spots.summary: Ye Olde Starre Inne is a historic public house on Stonegate in the city centre of York, England. The main block of the pub is a timber-framed structure, constructed in the 16th century, and a wing to its left was added in about 1600.

spots.name: St Olave's Church, York

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Olave's Church, York is a Grade I listed parish church of the Church of England in York. It stands on Marygate, by St Mary's Abbey.

spots.name: Roman Bath, York
spots.summary: The Roman Bath is a Grade II* listed public house on St Sampson's Square in the city of York, England. It is built above an ancient Roman bath house. The remains were uncovered during building work when the present pub was erected between 1929 and 1931 replacing an inn.

spots.name: Bar Convent

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Bar Convent Living Heritage Centre, at Micklegate Bar in York, England, was established in 1686 and is the oldest surviving Catholic convent in the British Isles. The laws of England at the time prohibited the foundation of Catholic convents, and as a result the community was both established and operated in secret.

spots.name: York Theatre Royal

hours.note: Closed Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri

spots.summary: York Theatre Royal is a theatre on St Leonard's Place, in York, England, which dates back to 1744. The theatre currently seats 750 people. Whilst the theatre is traditionally a proscenium theatre, it was reconfigured for a season in 2011 to offer productions in-the-round.

spots.name: All Saints, Pavement
spots.summary: All Saints' Church is a Grade I listed parish church in the Church of England on Pavement in the city of York. Services are from the Book of Common Prayer.

spots.name: Mansion House, York

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue

spots.summary: The Mansion House in York, England, is the working residence of the Lord Mayors of York during their term in office. It stands in St Helen's Square, where York's Coney Street and Lendal intersect in the city centre. It is built in an early Georgian style.

spots.name: The Retreat
spots.summary: The Retreat, commonly known as the York Retreat, is a place in England for the treatment of people with mental health needs. Located in Lamel Hill in York, it operates as a not for profit charitable organisation.

spots.name: York Assembly Rooms
spots.summary: The York Assembly Rooms on Blake Street, York, North Yorkshire, England, is a Grade I listed building designed by Lord Burlington in 1730 and completed in 1732.

spots.name: Heslington Hall
spots.summary: Heslington Hall is an historic manor house near the village of Heslington, North Yorkshire, England, within the city of York. The hall is part of the campus of the University of York.

spots.name: All Saints' Church
spots.summary: All Saints' Church is a Church of England parish church on North Street in the city of York. The church is a Grade I listed building.

spots.name: Kings Arms, York
spots.summary: The Kings Arms is a public house standing by the River Ouse in the city centre of York, England.

spots.name: Davygate
spots.summary: Davygate is a major shopping street in the city centre of York, in England.

spots.name: St Martin le Grand, York
spots.summary: St Martin le Grand is a Grade II* listed parish church in the Church of England in York.

spots.name: The Norman House

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Norman House is a scheduled monument and Grade I listed building in the city centre of York, England. Although in ruins, it has been described as "York's oldest house", dating from the late 12th century.

spots.name: Duncombe Place
spots.summary: Duncombe Place is a street in the city centre of York, in England.

spots.name: Holy Trinity Church, Micklegate, York

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Holy Trinity Church, Micklegate, York is a Grade I listed parish church in the Church of England in York.

spots.name: Coney Street
spots.summary: Coney Street is a major shopping street in the city centre of York, England. The street runs north-west from the junction of Spurriergate and Market Street, to St Helen's Square.

spots.name: Church of St Helen

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Helen's Church is a Grade II* listed parish church in the Church of England on Stonegate in the city of York.

spots.name: 35 Stonegate
spots.summary: 35 Stonegate is a Grade II* listed building in the city centre of York, England.

spots.name: Lendal Tower
spots.summary: Lendal Tower is a medieval tower that formed part of the city defences of York, England. It is located on the east bank of the River Ouse at the point where the river enters the walled city from the north-west. The building was used as a waterworks from 1616 until 1846 after which it was converted into offices.

spots.name: Newgate
spots.summary: Newgate is a street in the city centre of York, in England.

spots.name: Blake Street
spots.summary: Blake Street is a road in the city centre of York, in England.

spots.name: Grand Opera House
spots.summary: The Grand Opera House is a theatre on the corner of Clifford Street and Cumberland Street in York, England. The structure, which hosts touring productions of plays, musicals, opera and ballet, as well as one-off performances by comedians, and other theatrical and musical events, is a Grade II listed building.

spots.name: Church of St Michael

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Michael's Church is a Grade I listed former parish church in the Church of England, on Spurriergate in York, England.

spots.name: York City War Memorial
spots.summary: The York City War Memorial is a First World War memorial designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens and located in York in the north of England. Proposals for commemorating York's war dead originated in 1919 but proved controversial.

spots.name: Bishopthorpe Palace
spots.summary: Bishopthorpe Palace is the official residence of the Archbishop of York at Bishopthorpe, North Yorkshire, England. The palace is located on the River Ouse and is approximately 3 miles (4.8 km) south of York, which is the location of the diocese's cathedral, York Minster.

spots.name: 44 The Shambles
spots.summary: 44 The Shambles is a Grade II* listed building on The Shambles in York, England. Originating as a house in the late 15th century, it was refaced in the late 18th century and altered in the mid‑19th century, with further renovation in 1954. In 1968 it became part of the Central Historic Core conservation area.

spots.name: North Eastern Railway War Memorial
spots.summary: The North Eastern Railway War Memorial is a First World War memorial in York in northern England. It was designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens to commemorate employees of the North Eastern Railway (NER) who left to fight in the First World War and were killed while serving.

spots.summary: St Cuthbert's Church is a Grade I listed parish church in the Church of England on Peasholme Green in York, now known as The Well Prayer House.

spots.summary: Contact via [https://www.facebook.com/yorkarmymuseum Facebook] and [https://twitter.com/YorkArmyMuseum X]. The museum brings together the collections of one of the Army's oldest cavalry regiments - the Royal Dragoon Guards, dating from 1685, with one of its newest infantry regiments - the Yorkshire Regiment, which was only formed in 2006. spots.summary: Now the very apt home for the University of York's Archaeology Department, this was a royal headquarters during the Tudor and Stuart dynasties (16th and 17th centuries). As this is a working academic building, you may have to content yourself with admiring the Grade I listed architecture from the outside, unless you can pass as a scholar that is! spots.name: Micklegate Bar
spots.summary: Micklegate Bar was first recorded in the 12th century, but reuses stone from an earlier Roman gate. It has long been the official entrance to the city of York for royalty, and welcomed Queen Elizabeth II during her Diamond Jubilee celebrations in 2012. The indoor exhibition closed in 2025, but you can still view the very impressive exterior.

spots.name: Cold War Bunker

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu

spots.summary: From the 1960s to the 1990s, behind blast-proof doors, sat volunteers of the Royal Observer Corps, waiting to log nuclear bomb explosions in the region and monitor radioactive fallout. Fortunately they had a quiet few decades at the office. It is now English Heritage's most modern property, and also one of its spookiest.
